def-stratified-sampling-design-and-estim:
## Definition

Let $(U,y)$ be a finite population as in
[[def-finite-population-and-sampling-design]], and let
$U_1,\ldots,U_H$ be a finite partition of $U$ into nonempty strata. Write
$N_h=|U_h|$ and $N=\sum_{h=1}^H N_h$. Choose integers
$1\le n_h\le N_h$. In stratum $h$, draw $R_h$ by SRSWOR of size $n_h$ as in
[[def-simple-random-sampling-without-replacement]], independently across
strata. Thus the joint probability of a tuple $(r_1,\ldots,r_H)$ is
$$\prod_{h=1}^H\binom{N_h}{n_h}^{-1},$$
and its sample in $U$ is $R=\bigcup_{h=1}^H r_h$. This is the
**stratified SRSWOR design**. The union map is one-to-one because the strata
are disjoint; the support has $\prod_h\binom{N_h}{n_h}$ elements, so the
displayed mass function sums to one.

The fixed mean in stratum $h$ is
$$\bar y_h=\frac1{N_h}\sum_{i\in U_h}y_i.$$
For a noncertainty stratum ($n_h<N_h$), necessarily $N_h>1$, and its finite-
population variance is
$$S_h^2=\frac1{N_h-1}\sum_{i\in U_h}(y_i-\bar y_h)^2.$$
For every noncertainty stratum write $S_h=\sqrt{S_h^2}$ for its nonnegative
population standard deviation. For a realized sample, set
$$\bar y_{h,R}=\frac1{n_h}\sum_{i\in R_h}y_i,\qquad \widehat T_{st}=\sum_{h=1}^H N_h\bar y_{h,R}.$$
The quantity $\widehat T_{st}$ is the **stratified total estimator**. When
$n_h=N_h$, the stratum is a certainty stratum and its contribution is the
fixed total $N_h\bar y_h$; no $S_h^2$ is needed for that term. The population
values $y_i$ remain fixed: only the sample selections are random.
thm-stratified-total-unbiasedness-and-va:
## Statement

Let $(U,y)$ be a finite population with a partition and stratified SRSWOR
design as in [[def-stratified-sampling-design-and-estimator]]. Under the
design probability $P_d$, the stratified total estimator satisfies
$$E_d[\widehat T_{st}]=\sum_{i\in U}y_i.$$
Its design variance is
$$\operatorname{Var}_d(\widehat T_{st})=\sum_{h:n_h<N_h}N_h^2\left(1-\frac{n_h}{N_h}\right)\frac{S_h^2}{n_h}.$$
Thus certainty strata contribute zero and require no within-stratum variance
term.
thm-neyman-allocation-minimizes-stratifi:
## Statement

Use the notation of [[def-stratified-sampling-design-and-estimator]] and
[[thm-stratified-total-unbiasedness-and-variance]]. Let $J$ be a nonempty set
of noncertainty strata whose allocations vary, and suppose $S_h>0$ for each
$h\in J$, where $S_h:=\sqrt{S_h^2}$ is the positive population standard
deviation. Hold all other stratum allocations fixed. For real $x_h>0$ with
$\sum_{h\in J}x_h=n^\star>0$, consider the uncapped continuous relaxation
of the variance expression
$$V_0+\sum_{h\in J}N_h^2\left(1-\frac{x_h}{N_h}\right)\frac{S_h^2}{x_h},$$
where $V_0$ collects the fixed strata's variance terms. Its unique minimum
over this positive simplex is attained at
$$x_h=n^\star\frac{N_hS_h}{\sum_{k\in J}N_kS_k}\qquad(h\in J).$$
This is the continuous Neyman allocation. The relaxation imposes no integer,
capacity, lower-bound, or minimum-sample constraints; if the displayed
allocation violates a design constraint, it is not itself an admissible
stratified SRSWOR design.
thm-cost-optimal-stratified-allocation:
## Statement

Use the notation of [[def-stratified-sampling-design-and-estimator]] and
[[thm-stratified-total-unbiasedness-and-variance]]. Let $J$ be a nonempty set
of variable noncertainty strata with $S_h>0$, and hold all other allocations
fixed. Assign each $h\in J$ a positive per-unit cost $c_h$. For a fixed positive residual cost
budget $C^\star$, the uncapped continuous relaxation of the stratified
variance expression under $\sum_{h\in J}c_hx_h=C^\star$ has the unique
minimum
$$x_h=C^\star\frac{N_hS_h/\sqrt{c_h}}{\sum_{k\in J}N_kS_k\sqrt{c_k}}\qquad(h\in J).$$
Thus $x_h\propto N_hS_h/\sqrt{c_h}$. As in the fixed-size result, this
continuous formula does not enforce integer, capacity, lower-bound, or
minimum-sample constraints.
